description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and the accuracy (ACC, %) (y-axis) for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10⁴, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear and spans from 60% to 80%, with tick marks at 60, 65, 70, 75, and 80. The “Base” method (black line with circle markers) shows a steady increase from approximately 61% at co-occurrence 1 to about 67% at 10⁴. “FT” (blue line with downward triangle markers) rises from ~63% to ~68.5%. “IKE” (red line with upward triangle markers) increases from ~64.5% to ~70%. “MEND” (brown line with diamond markers) starts at ~66% and climbs to ~74%. “MEMIT” (purple line with circle markers) begins at ~66.5% and reaches ~72.5%. “ROME” (green line with square markers) starts at ~72.5% and plateaus near 77.5% after 10², showing the highest and most stable performance across the range. All lines exhibit upward trends, with ROME consistently outperforming the others, especially at higher co-occurrence numbers.
